title: readonly vs disabled
name: Readonly vs disabled — Spectrum
rule: Disabled = field exists but is unavailable. If the value must still be shown and copied, use read-only, not disabled.
pass_when: Unavailable fields are disabled. Values that must remain visible and copyable are read-only.
fail_when: A value that must be copied is in a disabled field.
overview: Disabled means unavailable; read-only keeps a value visible and copyable.
apply_when: Deciding whether a shown value must stay copyable or the field is unavailable.
not_when: Truly unavailable fields with no value users need to read or copy.
agent_hint: Use read-only when the value must stay visible and copyable; disable only if unavailable.
description: Spectrum separates disabled from read-only: disabled means the field exists but is unavailable, while read-only keeps a value on screen so users can still read and copy it. Putting a must-copy value in a disabled field blocks selection and fails the split. Use disabled for unavailable inputs; switch to read-only whenever the content still matters after interaction is locked.
do_not_claim: Fluent disabled-label-stays-perceivable as a merge; picker read-only (see `spectrum.picker-readonly-only-if-selection`). Overlap with extra 73: `fluent.disabled-field-label-stays-perceivable`.
